title: Arteannuin B, a sesquiterpene lactone from Artemisia annua, attenuates inflammatory response by inhibiting the ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2D3-mediated NF-kappaB activation.
authors: Chen, Hongqing; Hu, Qiongying; Wen, Tian; Luo, Liuling; Liu, Lu; Wang, Lun; Shen, Xiaofei
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究青蒿素B通过共价结合泛素结合酶UBE2D3抑制NF-κB通路发挥抗炎作用，核心是药物-蛋白互作，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anomalous activation of NF-kappaB signaling is associated with many inflammatory disorders, such as ulcerative colitis (UC) and acute lung injury (ALI). NF-kappaB activation requires the ubiquitination of receptor-interacting protein 1 (RIP1) and NF-kappaB essential modulator (NEMO). Therefore, inhibition of ubiquitation of RIP1 and NEMO may serve as a potential approach for inhibiting NF-kappaB activation and alleviating inflammatory disorders. PURPOSE: Here, we identified arteannuin B (ATB), a sesquiterpene lactone found in the traditional Chinese medicine Artemisia annua that is used to treat malaria and inflammatory diseases, as a potent anti-inflammatory compound, and then characterized the putative mechanisms of its anti-inflammatory action. METHODS: Detections of inflammatory mediators and cytokines in LPS- or TNF-alpha-stimulated murine macrophages using RT-qPCR, ELISA, and western blotting, respectively. Western blotting, CETSA, DARTS, MST, gene knockdown, LC-MS/MS, and molecular docking were used to determine the potential target and molecular mechanism of ATB. The pharmacological effects of ATB were further evaluated in DSS-induced colitis and LPS-induced ALI in vivo. RESULTS: ATB effectively diminished the generation of NO and PGE(2) by down-regulating iNOS and COX2 expression, and decreased the mRNA expression and release of IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha in LPS-exposed RAW264.7 macrophages. The anti-inflammatory effect of ATB was further demonstrated in LPS-treated BMDMs and TNF-alpha-activated RAW264.7 cells. We further found that ATB obviously inhibited NF-kappaB activation induced by LPS or TNF-alpha in vitro. Moreover, compared with ATB, dihydroarteannuin B (DATB) which lost the unsaturated double bond, completely failed to repress LPS-induced NO release and NF-kappaB activation in vitro. Furthermore, UBE2D3, a ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, was identified as the functional target of ATB, but not DATB. UBE2D3 knockdown significantly abolished ATB-mediated inhibition on LPS-induced NO production. Mechanistically, ATB could covalently bind to the catalytic cysteine 85 of UBE2D3, thereby inhibiting the function of UBE2D3 and preventing ubiquitination of RIP1 and NEMO. In vivo, ATB treatment exhibited robust protective effects against DSS-induced UC and LPS-induced ALI. CONCLUSION: Our findings first demonstrated that ATB exerted anti-inflammatory functions by repression of NF-kappaB pathway via covalently binding to UBE2D3, and raised the possibility that ATB could be effective in the treatment of inflammatory diseases and other diseases associated with abnormal NF-kappaB activation.
abstract_zh: 背景：NF-kappaB信号的异常激活与多种炎症性疾病相关，如溃疡性结肠炎（UC）和急性肺损伤（ALI）。NF-kappaB的激活需要受体相互作用蛋白1（RIP1）和NF-kappaB必需调节因子（NEMO）的泛素化。因此，抑制RIP1和NEMO的泛素化可能作为抑制NF-kappaB激活和缓解炎症性疾病的潜在策略。目的：在此，我们鉴定出青蒿素B（ATB），一种存在于传统中药青蒿（Artemisia annua）中的倍半萜内酯，用于治疗疟疾和炎症性疾病，作为一种有效的抗炎化合物，并进一步表征其抗炎作用的潜在机制。方法：分别使用RT-qPCR、ELISA和western blotting检测LPS或TNF-alpha刺激的小鼠巨噬细胞中的炎症介质和细胞因子。使用western blotting、CETSA、DARTS、MST、基因敲低、LC-MS/MS和分子对接来确定ATB的潜在靶点和分子机制。在体内，进一步评估了ATB对DSS诱导的结肠炎和LPS诱导的ALI的药理作用。结果：ATB通过下调iNOS和COX2表达有效减少NO和PGE(2)的产生，并降低LPS暴露的RAW264.7巨噬细胞中IL-1beta、IL-6和TNF-alpha的mRNA表达和释放。ATB的抗炎作用在LPS处理的BMDMs和TNF-alpha激活的RAW264.7细胞中进一步得到证实。我们进一步发现，ATB在体外明显抑制LPS或TNF-alpha诱导的NF-kappaB激活。此外，与ATB相比，失去不饱和双键的二氢青蒿素B（DATB）在体外完全无法抑制LPS诱导的NO释放和NF-kappaB激活。进一步地，UBE2D3，一种泛素结合酶，被鉴定为ATB的功能靶点，而非DATB。UBE2D3敲低显著消除了ATB介导的对LPS诱导的NO产生的抑制。机制上，ATB可以共价结合到UBE2D3的催化半胱氨酸85，从而抑制UBE2D3的功能并阻止RIP1和NEMO的泛素化。在体内，ATB治疗对DSS诱导的UC和LPS诱导的ALI表现出强大的保护作用。结论：我们的发现首次证明ATB通过共价结合UBE2D3抑制NF-kappaB通路发挥抗炎功能，并提出ATB可能在治疗炎症性疾病及其他与异常NF-kappaB激活相关的疾病中具有有效性。
